title: SEC-TESTS: round 1 summary — tests passing review
description:
Tests passing review with independent oracles and adequate coverage:

bt5.1 (fault_queue_full.rs): Oracle is RFC 4644 §2.5 and RFC 977 §3.8. Tests use a real peering session over loopback TCP with a pre-filled queue. All three sub-cases tested (TAKETHIS→431, IHAVE→436, positive control→239). The metric counter (rejected_full_total) is verified to increment, proving the article was not silently accepted. Verdict: ADEQUATE.

bt5.8 (server.rs bearer+basic tests): Oracle is RFC 6750 §2.1 and §3.1. Five scenarios cover the interaction matrix: Basic-only, well-formed-but-unknown Bearer (must reject, not fall through), malformed Bearer (falls through to Basic), sequential requests, valid Bearer wins over Basic. All five use a live HTTP server over loopback. Verdict: ADEQUATE.

bt5.11 (hlc.rs overflow tests): Oracle is Kulkarni & Demirbas 2014 HLC algorithm invariant: result must be strictly greater than the pre-overflow seed. Three sub-cases for send(), receive(), and post-overflow receive(). All use deterministic seeded inputs. Verdict: ADEQUATE (with fragility note filed separately as stoa-6b816309.21).

bt5.12 (mime_parser.rs boundary tests): Oracle is RFC 2046 §5.1.1 and RFC 2045 §6.7 (QP example) and RFC 4648 §10 (base64 'foobar' vector). Four boundary tests: bare-LF, mixed CRLF+LF, mid-line boundary (must not split), prefix false positive (--boundaryFOO must not match). Verdict: ADEQUATE on the boundary tests; QP oracle has a CID lookup self-reference noted separately in stoa-6b816309.23.

bt5.7 (sieve): The integration test (test_sieve_compile_error_sends_451) is structurally sound — it exercises the full SMTP session, checks 451 appears after 354, and verifies 0 messages delivered. Verdict: ADEQUATE at integration level; unit-level assertion weakness noted in stoa-6b816309.16.

bt5.10 (ingestion.rs): case_insensitive_msgid_duplicate_detected tests the duplicate detection path. Verdict: ADEQUATE for the detection direction; insert-direction normalization gap noted in stoa-6b816309.18.

Tests with open findings requiring follow-up:
- bt5.3: stoa-6b816309.10 (max_age_days end-to-end path not tested in GcRunner)
- bt5.5: stoa-6b816309.11 (epoch error path has no test)
- bt5.6: stoa-6b816309.13 (key length error path has no test)
- bt5.7: stoa-6b816309.16 (unit assertion too weak)
- bt5.10: stoa-6b816309.18 (insert-direction normalization not tested)
- bt5.12: stoa-6b816309.23 (QP oracle CID lookup self-reference)
